## Tours visiting Casa Aliaga: how Lima opens a journey through the Andes

The [excursion through Miraflores, Love Park and Casa Aliaga](/peru/lima/lima-miraflores-casa-aliaga/) introduces two contrasting sides of [Lima](/peru/place/lima/). In the morning, you can see the Pacific coastline and modern neighbourhoods before moving on to the architecture of the historic centre and one of the city's oldest inhabited houses.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} visiting Casa Aliaga. On a multi-day journey, it is important to consider **where the excursion falls in the itinerary**, as travellers may depart for the highlands on the same day.

## When Casa Aliaga is visited on the Peru and Bolivia itinerary

On the [10-day “Enchanting Peru and Bolivia” tour](/multi-country/tour/enchanted-peru-bolivia-10-days/), the Lima excursion is scheduled for **day two**, starting at 09:00. After sightseeing in the city, the programme includes a transfer to the airport and a flight to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/).

The excursion takes in Miraflores, Love Park and the historic centre, including the Main Square and Casa Aliaga. The wider itinerary then continues to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), across the Andes to [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), and onwards to Bolivia's attractions: Copacabana, the Island of the Sun and La Paz.

On this journey, the walk through Lima is the opening cultural chapter. It introduces the history of a Spanish colonial city before visits to Inca monuments and highland settlements.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_peru_bolivia_enchanted_10_days}}

## Why Casa Aliaga is worth particular attention

Casa Aliaga is a historic mansion near Lima's main square. Its history has been connected to the Aliaga family since the 16th century. Rebuilt after earthquakes, the building reflects different periods in the Peruvian capital's development. Interior rooms and architectural details offer a glimpse into the life of a prosperous city residence during the colonial and republican eras.

Including this house distinguishes the programme from a standard sightseeing tour. The [four-hour city tour](/peru/lima/lima-city-tour-4-hours/) also visits Miraflores and the historic centre but gives additional attention to Huaca Pucllana and the Santo Domingo Monastery. Its primary aim is an overview of the city's districts and historical periods.

| Excursion | Main focus |
|---|---|
| [Casa Aliaga](/peru/lima/lima-miraflores-casa-aliaga/) | Historic mansion |
| [Four-hour city tour](/peru/lima/lima-city-tour-4-hours/) | Districts and monuments |
| [Folklore dinner](/peru/lima/lima-folklore-dinner-show/) | Evening performance |

The final option suits a different time of day: it includes dinner and a folklore show, rather than a morning introduction to the city's landmarks.

## Planning the excursion before the flight to Cusco

The most time-sensitive aspect of day two is coordinating the house visit, departure from the historic centre, the drive to the airport and flight check-in. On this tour, the excursion begins at 09:00. On other trips, timing is agreed according to the itinerary and air tickets.

After coastal Lima, the route proceeds to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), which stands at a much higher altitude. When planning the following walks, allow time for rest and consider how participants feel. This is especially important on a journey that continues through high-altitude parts of Peru and Bolivia.

The tour has different accommodation packages and specific conditions for participants. See the prices and hotel arrangements in the [current “Enchanting Peru and Bolivia” programme](/multi-country/tour/enchanted-peru-bolivia-10-days/); one rate should not be applied to every option.

## What to check when choosing the itinerary

The ten-day tour includes transfers, excursions with a Russian-speaking guide along the route and museum admissions as specified in the programme. When confirming arrangements, check exactly which interior visits form part of the Lima outing, how admission to Casa Aliaga is handled and how much time is allocated for exploring it.

Also check the domestic flight time, the city where the entire journey ends and the terms of optional excursions. A two-country trip requires a separate review of entry documents and rules for each traveller's nationality. The [Peru tour catalogue](/peru/tour/) offers shorter options without continuing into Bolivia.

## Frequently asked questions about tours including Casa Aliaga

### On which day is the house visited?

On the [10-day Peru and Bolivia programme](/multi-country/tour/enchanted-peru-bolivia-10-days/), the excursion takes place on day two before the flight to Cusco.

### Are Casa Aliaga and Huaca Pucllana the same place?

No. Casa Aliaga is a historic colonial-era house, while Huaca Pucllana is a pre-Columbian archaeological complex. They illuminate different periods of Lima's history.

### Can Casa Aliaga be replaced by a standard city tour?

These are two separate excursion products with different emphases. A substitution must be agreed within the particular multi-day itinerary.

### In which language is the excursion conducted?

The ten-day itinerary specifies excursions with a Russian-speaking guide. The language for the particular city outing is confirmed when arranging the trip.

## Pachacamac from Lima: the Temple of the Sun and an ancient sanctuary in four hours

[Pachacamac](/peru/place/pachacamac/) lies in the Lurín River valley south of [Lima](/peru/place/lima/). Temple structures, palaces and plazas built during different periods long before the Spanish conquest survive among the dry hills. This outing suits travellers who want to explore Peru's pre-Columbian history beyond the capital's museums and colonial streets.

Ada Tours offers a **four-hour excursion** with **transfers and a guide speaking English or Spanish**. The itinerary names the Temple of the Sun, Acllawasi, Taurichumbi Palace and the Pilgrims' Plaza. Lunch and medical insurance are not included.

## Why Pachacamac mattered in ancient Peru

The sanctuary developed over many centuries, long before the expansion of the Inca state. Pilgrims visited the site, whose religious buildings were associated with the worship of the deity Pachacamac. Different coastal societies left their own architectural features here, so the complex cannot be reduced to the Inca period alone.

After the region became part of the Inca Empire, new structures appeared. The Temple of the Sun, on higher ground, became one of the most prominent buildings of that period. Against sandy slopes and the ocean, its adobe walls contrast with the stone architecture of highland [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/).

At Pachacamac, it is particularly interesting to observe not only individual temples but also how temple terraces, squares and residential or administrative buildings relate to one another. Such a route helps visitors imagine a pilgrimage centre with permanent infrastructure.

## What the archaeological route includes

**The Temple of the Sun** stands on elevated ground. This part of the complex offers views of the dry valley and coast. The building is associated with the Inca period, while its present condition reflects the monument's age and conservation work.

**Acllawasi** (the "house of chosen women") forms part of Pachacamac's historic ensemble. Its function is studied using archaeological evidence and comparative information about the Inca era, so scholars may interpret some aspects of the building differently.

**Taurichumbi Palace** and **the Pilgrims' Plaza** reveal other aspects of how the sanctuary was organised: its administrative and ceremonial functions. The plaza makes it particularly clear that the site drew not only priests and local inhabitants but large numbers of visitors.

The site has an archaeological museum displaying objects and information on the history of excavations. It helps explain the complex, but **neither a museum admission ticket nor a guaranteed separate museum visit is specified among the included services**. Access to particular sections also depends on conservation rules.

## Excursion prices and inclusions

We offer different rates according to group size.

| Participants | Listed price |
|---|---|
| Base rate | **$230** |
| 2 people | **$119 per person** |
| 3 people | **$83 per person** |
| 4 people | **$77 per person** |

The base **$230** rate is stated without a separate clarification of its pricing unit. For 2, 3 and 4 participants, the price is expressly quoted per person. A rate for one group size must not be applied to another.

Included are **transfers** and **an English- or Spanish-speaking guide**. **Lunch and medical insurance** are paid separately. Admission tickets to the archaeological complex are not named in the included-services list; confirm this point before visiting.

## Preparing for the four-hour outing

Pachacamac stands in an arid, exposed landscape. Much of the route is in sunlight, with dirt tracks and uneven surfaces. Bring water, a hat, sun protection and closed shoes.

For travellers with limited mobility, it is important to agree on an accessible sequence of stops beforehand: the archaeological complex is extensive, and some areas have slopes or steps. When choosing the time, account for the drive from Lima and the site's opening arrangements on that date.

If you also want to discover monuments from a different period, combine the trip with a visit to the historic centre of [Lima](/peru/place/lima/) or browse [Peru's cultural and historical tours](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/peru/). These are different excursion themes: Pachacamac is principally about the coast's pre-Hispanic heritage.

## Frequently asked questions about the Pachacamac excursion

### How long is the excursion?

Our excursion lasts **four hours**. The exact departure and return times are agreed according to your accommodation and traffic conditions.

### What languages does the guide speak?

**English or Spanish** is available. Russian-language guiding has not been confirmed for this programme.

### Is lunch included?

No. Lunch and medical insurance are expressly listed among services excluded from the price.

### What does the outing cost for two people?

For 2 participants, the stated rate is **$119 per person**. For 3 participants, it is $83 per person; for 4, $77 per person.

### Is the site suitable for walking in hot weather?

The route passes through dry, exposed terrain. Bring water and sun protection and agree in advance on how long to remain outdoors.

## Lima: from the colonial centre to San Isidro and Miraflores

This sightseeing excursion introduces several parts of [Lima](/peru/place/lima/) in one sequence. We begin with the colonial landmarks of the historic centre, then continue through [San Isidro](/peru/place/san-isidro-lima/) and [Miraflores](/peru/place/miraflores-lima/). The route ends with a return to the hotel.

## Main Square, cathedral and San Francisco Monastery

In the historic centre, you visit [Lima's Main Square](/peru/place/plaza-mayor-lima/) with the [cathedral](/peru/place/lima-cathedral/) and [San Francisco Monastery](/peru/place/san-francisco-monastery-lima/). Along the way, you see colonial buildings with traditional wooden balconies. These details bring the city into focus through individual façades and public spaces.

San Francisco is a monastic complex in Lima's historic centre. If you are interested in its catacombs or particular interiors, we will confirm the visit's scope and access requirements before booking.

## San Isidro and Miraflores

In San Isidro, you see an olive grove, the Country Club and a golf course. This part of the journey offers a change of scenery after the colonial centre: the route passes through a residential district with green spaces. Viewing the golf course does not mean playing golf or receiving a separate sporting service.

Next, we travel to Miraflores. Here the programme includes Central Park, the Town Hall and the main shopping streets, including Larco Avenue. This refers specifically to Larco Avenue in Miraflores; a visit to the Larco Museum belongs to another excursion programme.

## The excursion on the final day of a longer journey

On our [15-day tour of Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Peru](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/), Lima sightseeing takes place in the morning of day fifteen, after breakfast. The previous day, you arrive from Cusco and check into a hotel. After the excursion, you return to the hotel before heading to the airport for your international flight.

Consider this sequence when planning your flight: sightseeing occupies part of the departure day, so the airport transfer follows it. We agree the precise excursion start time, guide language and separate-booking price for your chosen date.

## Frequently asked questions

### Which districts are included?

We visit Lima's historic centre, San Isidro and Miraflores. Each district has specific stops described in the excursion.

### Which monastery will we visit?

San Francisco is included in this excursion. Access to individual interior rooms is confirmed when arranging the trip.

### Is there a return to the hotel?

Yes. The excursion returns to the hotel. As part of the 15-day tour, an airport transfer then follows.

## Tours including San Francisco, San Isidro and Miraflores

This selection features journeys with our [Lima sightseeing excursion](/peru/lima/san-francisco-san-isidro-miraflores/). The route connects the Main Square and cathedral, [San Francisco Monastery](/peru/place/san-francisco-monastery-lima/), the [San Isidro](/peru/place/san-isidro-lima/) district with its olive grove, and Miraflores with Central Park and shopping streets.

## Lima at the end of a four-country journey

Our [15-day tour of Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Peru](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/) begins in Rio de Janeiro. After Iguazu, Buenos Aires, Santiago and Chile's coastline, you continue through Peru: the Sacred Valley, Machu Picchu and Cusco, followed by Lima.

You fly to Lima on day fourteen after an excursion to the archaeological sites of Cusco. On arrival, the programme provides a welcome, transfer and hotel check-in. The final night of the journey is spent in the Peruvian capital.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_braziliya_argentina_chili_peru_ru}}

## What happens on the final day

After breakfast, we set out for sightseeing. In the historic centre, you visit the [Main Square](/peru/place/plaza-mayor-lima/) and [cathedral](/peru/place/lima-cathedral/), along with San Francisco Monastery. The programme then continues to San Isidro and [Miraflores](/peru/place/miraflores-lima/).

At the end of the excursion, you return to the hotel. The next stage is the transfer to the airport for an international flight. When choosing tickets, remember that a sightseeing programme is scheduled before airport departure; its exact time must fit the flight.

## Accommodation, excursions and flights

The 15-day tour includes 14 hotel nights with breakfast, transfers and excursions along the route, entrance tickets and the Vistadome train to Machu Picchu. Accommodation rates appear on the tour page.

International and domestic flights are paid separately. The Peruvian section includes a Cusco–Lima flight; before that, the itinerary visits the Sacred Valley and Machu Picchu. Choose the final city and return airport accordingly, since the journey ends in Lima.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is there a Lima excursion before departure?

Yes. Day fifteen includes the historic centre, San Isidro and Miraflores, followed by a return to the hotel and an airport transfer.

### How many nights are spent in Lima?

There is one night in Lima on this itinerary, after arrival from Cusco and before the final sightseeing excursion.

### Can we rely on the price in the tour table alone?

The table shows the current tour price, but air tickets are separate. Include both domestic and international flights when calculating the total cost.

## Machu Picchu excursions: comparing routes and formats

A visit to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) begins long before entering the ancient citadel. You must determine your departure point, the train to the Aguas Calientes area, the ascent to the ruins and the entry circuit available to you. That is why two excursions to the same destination can be very different in logistics and experience.

We offer, among other options, **a guided excursion from Aguas Calientes** and **an extended programme aboard the Hiram Bingham train**. Both explore Inca history, but suit different travel preferences.

## Classic guided excursion from Aguas Calientes

[“Machu Picchu from Aguas Calientes with a Guide”](/peru/aguas-calientes/machu-picchu-from-aguas-calientes/) suits visitors who are already in [Aguas Calientes](/peru/place/aguas-calientes/) or have included a rail journey there in their main itinerary.

Our programme includes an approximately **30-minute** bus ride up to Machu Picchu, followed by a guided visit to the archaeological complex. Its main appeal is the chance to explore stone buildings, terraces, temples and residential areas against a mountainous backdrop.

This option is particularly convenient with an overnight stay in Aguas Calientes, when the journey from Cusco has already taken place. However, the existence of an excursion starting in town **does not confirm** that the train ticket from Cusco, accommodation, entrance ticket or every transfer is included in that excursion. Compare each service against the chosen tour's terms.

## Hiram Bingham train and an excursion with afternoon tea

[“Machu Picchu by Hiram Bingham with Tea at Sanctuary Lodge”](/peru/machu-picchu/machu-picchu-hiram-bingham-sanctuary-tea/) is a separate, extended product. It begins with a transfer to Ollantaytambo station and a journey on the **Hiram Bingham (Belmond)** train. After arriving in Aguas Calientes, travellers take a shared bus to the archaeological site entrance.

Inside the complex, there is a **private excursion with a Russian-speaking guide lasting about 2.5 hours**. Afterwards, afternoon tea is served at the Sanctuary Lodge restaurant near the entrance to Machu Picchu. The return journey aboard the Hiram Bingham includes dinner on board, followed by a transfer from Poroy to Cusco.

This programme suits those who want the train journey and on-route service to be a major part of the day. It is different from an excursion starting directly in Aguas Calientes. The precise inclusions must be checked against the chosen programme, and prices and availability for the chosen date agreed under that product's terms.

| Option | Defining features |
|---|---|
| From Aguas Calientes | Ascent and guided tour |
| Hiram Bingham | Train, guide and afternoon tea |

## Admission tickets and the route through the citadel

Machu Picchu is a protected archaeological site with a special visitor-entry system. **Admission tickets are tied to a date, time and specific sightseeing route.** The official Peruvian Ministry of Culture platform, Tuboleto, offers a choice of visiting circuit, route and admission time.

This is crucial when booking an excursion: the name “Machu Picchu” does not automatically mean access to every temple, terrace and panoramic viewpoint. Some routes emphasise classic views from above, while others spend more time inside the complex. Access to individual features depends on the ticket purchased.

Before travelling, coordinate the ticket, guided tour, train and bus as a single sequence. If one element is booked for a conflicting time, problems may arise when transferring between them. Rules and permitted circuits change, so use the official ticket for the specific date rather than an incidental diagram from previous years.

## What you will see during the excursion

The Historic Sanctuary of Machu Picchu is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The complex stands at approximately **2,430 metres** among the mountains of the eastern Andes. Inca stone structures, steps, agricultural terraces and ceremonial spaces survive here.

Well-known landmarks include the Temple of the Sun, Temple of the Three Windows, Main Temple and Intihuatana stone. However, the exact route is determined by your admission ticket, so the mention of a landmark in a general site description does not guarantee access during a particular excursion.

A guide's main value is explaining how the settlement, agricultural terraces and engineering systems worked on steep terrain. This differs from taking a quick, independent look at the panorama.

## Where to start: Cusco or Aguas Calientes?

From [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), travellers usually reach Machu Picchu via the Sacred Valley and a railway journey to Aguas Calientes. Some programmes include a stop at [Ollantaytambo](/peru/place/ollantaytambo/), where the rail portion begins. Train schedules, departure stations and road transfers must be confirmed for the specific date.

If you are already staying in Aguas Calientes, an excursion departing from there is more convenient. If your goal is a full day featuring a luxury train journey and return to Cusco, consider the extended Hiram Bingham programme.

Trying to fit all neighbouring attractions, an additional mountain ascent and a long citadel tour into one day without checking train times and tickets is risky. For a longer [Peru tour](/peru/tour/), first decide where Machu Picchu falls in the overall programme and then choose the excursion format.

## Weather and physical effort

Machu Picchu is in mountainous terrain where rain, fog and slippery stone steps are possible. Even a relatively short visit involves walking over uneven surfaces, using stairways and negotiating changes in elevation. Comfortable shoes and rain protection are particularly important.

Local weather varies by season and throughout the day. Clouds may obscure the mountain views, so no ticket or excursion format can guarantee a clear panorama. Travellers who find stone steps difficult should check the accessibility of their chosen circuit and discuss any health limitations before booking.

## Frequently asked questions about Machu Picchu excursions

### Must I choose a visiting route when buying a ticket?

Yes. The Peruvian Ministry of Culture's official ticketing system requires a choice of visiting circuit, route, date and entry time.

### How does an excursion from Aguas Calientes differ from Hiram Bingham?

The first focuses on getting up to the citadel and exploring it with a guide. The second includes the longer Hiram Bingham train journey, a private guided visit, afternoon tea and a return trip with dinner, as described in our programme.

### Can one ticket give access to every temple?

Not necessarily. The temples, terraces and viewpoints available depend on the selected circuit. Check your ticket's access conditions before booking a guided excursion.

### Should I reserve a separate day for Machu Picchu?

It is sensible to allocate a substantial part of a day to this site. Transport, the bus to the entrance, ticket checks and sightseeing need coordinated timing; whether everything fits in one day depends on where you stay overnight and which programme you choose.
